volt1geur.text: Volt1geur fights at the very top of the tracked population, with a matchup rating and resistance both among the very best. The pace is measured rather than frantic, and the headshot share is thin, yet the matchup kill-death line stays near the top. The lifetime board undersells the whole picture, painting a far lower IvI than the matchups support.

valrynnc.text: ValrynNC brings volume and venom: the lifetime kill-death line sits in the highest tier, and the matchups back it up. The trigger keeps a good clip, the edge stays strong while the opposition gets tougher, and the kept share holds firm against the strongest third. A strong regular with a ledger to match.

verylowskillsandveryfewkills.text: VeryLowSkillsandVeryFewKills has been at this since 2012, and the card reads like a long apprenticeship paid off: matchup rating and bravery up near the very top, resistance higher still, plus a matchup kill-death mark to match. Pace sits comfortably in the top ranks, the aim is precise, as the lifetime board puts them a little below the matchups. The one soft note is headshot share, merely middling, but the results speak for themselves.

vsaier.text: VSaier plays a precise, high-tempo game: the rating is top-rank, and so are activity, bravery, and resistance, with pace to match. The aim sits in the top ranks, though the headshot share runs mid-pack, and the lifetime ledger marks them a notch below the matchups. The strongest third drops the game below the pack — the soft seam in a strong card.

vocaloidia.text: VocaloidIA has been at this since 2015, and the craft is plain: the matchup kill-death mark sits in the upper tier, and so do rating, tempo, bravery, and resistance. Accuracy sits top-shelf, the headshot share above average, and the lifetime IvI sits in the upper tier too. Consistency alone sits middling on a long, distinguished card.

voidy6vanu.text: Voidy6Vanu plays a complete, high-tempo game: rating, activity, and bravery all run near the very top, with output and resistance sitting close behind. The aim is sharp, headshots plentiful, and the results keep their shape as the opposition improves. The lifetime board rates them top-shelf too — every line on the card reads strong.

vindictusdefyingfate.text: VindictusDefyingFate earns every win twice over: at the top end of the matchup board, unshaken by quick-killing opposition, and a lifetime kill-death record near the top. The tempo runs above the middle, the aim ordinary, and the lifetime IvI lands mid-pack — the matchups tell the stronger story. Consistency against the hardest third holds up well, the quiet seal on a strong card.

varettte.text: Varettte arrived in 2026 and has taken no time settling in: a top-shelf rating, a scorching tempo, and headshots among the sharpest tracked. The lifetime numbers echo the matchups, and the grip stays firm in the hardest third. A rising fighter with the whole road ahead.

vsnb.text: VSnB wins matchups without ever looking rushed: a top-tier rating, resistance near the top, and a head-to-head kill-death line near the top. The pace sits mid-pack and headshots land below average, which keeps the card honest. The lifetime board tells a middling story beside the matchups, which carry the real weight.

vexarivs.text: VexariVS is a fresh name with a loud opening: in the upper tier of the matchup rankings, fast hands, and calm when the stakes climb. The accuracy is already precise, and the lifetime numbers back the matchups up. Early days, but the opening is hard to ignore.

vspingping.text: VSpingping plays at full throttle: upper-tier matchup rating, a tempo up near the top, with bravery that rises as the fighting hardens. The lifetime board backs the matchups across the card. The one wrinkle in a fast, fearless game: the edge dips against the hardest third.

vindictivetr.text: VindictiveTR plays a sharp, patient game: a matchup grade sitting with the best, bravery that stays rock-steady, and a tempo that stays brisk. The close-quarters kill-death count lands above average, the lifetime board agrees, and the accuracy and headshots both sit near the top. Take it as a sketch: the opponent pool behind it runs older and thinner.

valkyriexi3.text: ValkyrieXI3 plays a smooth, well-rounded game: well above average across the matchup board, steady as the opposition hardens, and quick to punish a mistake. The lifetime board paints a touch taller than the matchups do, and when the opposition gets toughest, the edge thins a little. Aim is ordinary, but the shots that connect tend to land where they count. A strong regular with no real hole in the game.

victorymom.text: VictoryMom picks the fights well: a duel kill-death tally near the top, with resistance that barely bends. When the opposition gets toughest, the edge falls away, and the headshot share sits below average. The lifetime board reads mid-pack, more modest than the matchups. A smart, careful game that shines brightest where the odds already lean friendly.

v3ctorfps.text: V3ctorfps plays with the throttle wide open: activity near the top, with bravery close behind, and a kill pace that runs with the fastest tracked. Headshots land near the top, the aim runs above average; the lifetime board sits near the top. The catch: when the pressure peaks, the edge falls away, the one soft spot on a fast, fearless card.

vysal.text: Vysal has been winning fights since 2012, and the card shows why: well clear of average in the matchups, bravery that keeps climbing as enemies get stronger, while resistance gives little ground. The duel kill-death figure sits well above average, and the lifetime numbers back the matchups. A veteran who still brings the pace.

vitoxmaximus.text: VITOXMAXIMUS has been winning fights since 2014, and the finish is the story: a matched-fight kill-death ratio near the top, with the lifetime kill-death line right beside it. Accuracy sits above average, yet headshots are scarce — the kills come from steady shooting, not snap headshots. The lifetime IvI board sits mid-pack, well short of the matchups, which makes the matchup card the honest read.

vanududebro.text: VANUDUDEBRO brings a quietly complete game: above average on nearly every line, from matchup rating to tempo to resistance, without a single glaring hole. The aim lands above average too, and the headshot share sits mid-pack. Consistency holds around the middle as well, so the card reads as a dependable regular who rarely beats themselves — and rarely gets beaten badly either.

verygoodplayertr.text: VeryGoodPlayerTR plays a clean, complete game: headshots near the top, and a matchup standing well above average. The tempo and nerve hold up, and the lifetime board points the same way. Drawn from a thinner, earlier pool of opponents, so read this one as a rough outline rather than a finished portrait.

voszakns.text: VoszakNS plays a solid, unspectacular game: matchup grade well above average, tempo and nerve to match, aim in the middle of the pack. The lifetime board lands mid-pack too, a touch below the matchups. A reliable regular, the kind who keeps the fight honest without ever chasing the spotlight.

vyss.text: Vyss has been fighting since 2012, and the matchups still rate them well above average: steady tempo, steady nerve, steady aim. The lifetime board is more modest, landing mid-pack instead. A long-serving regular whose matchup game keeps quietly outshining the lifetime ledger, season after season, without fuss.

vanitied.text: Vanitied has been on the board since 2026 and already plays like a fixture: accuracy near the top, headshots close behind, and a kill pace alongside, plus bravery that grows as the fighting toughens. The matchup rating comes in well above average; the lifetime board confirms the picture. The toughest-third line sits middling — the single ordinary line on a young, loud card.

vitoxxx.text: VITOXXX turns fights into wins at a near-top clip: the one-on-one kill-death tally sits near the top, backed by above-average rating, tempo and resistance. The headshot share runs below average, and the lifetime board sits below the matchups too. A veteran since 2014 whose duel record does the talking.

vexarinc.text: VexariNC is barely three weeks into the record and already turning heads: accuracy near the top, results that hold up against the hardest third, and a kill-death scoreboard from real battles sitting near the top. The matchup rating and lifetime IvI both sit near the top too. Early read, but the opening pages are hard to ignore.

vultoire.text: Vultoire has been at this since 2017, and the card shows a fighter who lives at full speed: sitting above the pack in the matchups, dauntless as the opposition hardens, and cruising at a top pace. The matchup kill ledger runs near the top, while the lifetime ledger echoes the matchups. Only the edge against the hardest third thins a little, the one wrinkle in a fast, complete card.

vulnerableshooter.text: Nothing about VulnerableShooter screams, and nothing sags either. Every line lands on the strong side — the matchup grade, the tempo, the bravery, the resistance, and the kill-death split from real opposition — with the lifetime board in step. The aim and the headshots sit squarely ordinary, and the edge stays put against the strongest third without ever stealing the show. A steady, unspectacular regular who makes every fight cost something.

vanguard2833.text: Vanguard2833 picks fights like a collector picks pieces: slow to arrive, brutally effective once there, and nearly impossible to dent. The faceoff arithmetic is ruthless, and the lifetime ledger sits low, underselling a card the matchups rate far higher. A patient, exacting regular who trades volume for verdicts and usually wins the trade.

veersling.text: Veersling has been fighting since 2012, and the card tells a long story: sitting clear of the middle on the matchup board, with resistance that stands up to stronger opposition and a lifetime kill-death ratio in the top tier. Against the hardest third the edge fades badly, and the lifetime rating sits below the middle. A veteran whose best work shows in the matchups, not the lifetime board.

vyssan.text: Vyssan plays a lively, front-foot game: well clear of the middle overall, a quick tempo, and fearless against stronger opposition. The aim is ordinary, the impact is not — a strong regular who keeps the pressure on and keeps the fight moving. The head-to-head ledger sits mid-pack, and the lifetime numbers agree with that picture.

vincenteve.text: VINCENTEVE plays a tidy, well-balanced game: a notch above the pack in the matchups, with steady aim and a tempo that keeps the pressure on. The matchup kill-death record sits mid-pack, the one quieter line in a strong card. The lifetime board tells the same story, marking a dependable regular who keeps every fight competitive.

valkerbalker.text: Valkerbalker plies a quiet, workmanlike craft: above average in the matchups, even-keeled as the opposition strengthens, and solid when the fighting gets harder. The head-to-head ledger sits above average, the pace stays middling, and the lifetime board runs a touch lower. A dependable regular who does the unglamorous work and does it well.

vshurri.text: VSHurri plays a fast, front-foot game that outruns the lifetime board: well above average in direct matchups, steady as the enemies get stronger, and fast enough to hold the pace. Headshots are rare, and the edge fades against the very best opposition, but the overall picture stays strong. A regular who brings tempo to every fight and leaves the other side chasing.

volgaaaa.text: Volgaaaa aims like few others on the board: well above average overall, brisk through the exchanges, and still pressing hard as the enemies get stronger, and the aim rides near the very top. The headshots land with the very best tracked, and the career ledger reads stronger still than the matchups. Against the very best opposition, the edge gives a little — the one blemish on a sharp game. A precise, punishing regular who makes every shot count.

vexaritr.text: VexariTR has only been around a month and already plays like a headline act: top-shelf tempo, a matchup record near the very top, and aim that lands where it counts. The lifetime figures are just as loud, with accuracy and headshots both sitting at the summit. A fresh account, so the story is young — but the first pages already sing.
